first_hunter_context.bar: Total revenue: company guide $197.0-202.0B (Q2 release, 2026-07-30), consensus $202.2B. Two sources agree on the consensus: 24/7 Wall St (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/amazon-slides-3-as-alphabets-12-plunge-raises-stakes-for-aws-report-meta-rises-3-microsoft-pulls-back/, $202.25B, EPS $1.97) and Pepperstone (https://pepperstone.com/en/insights/market-analysis/equities/amazon-q3-2026-earnings-preview, ~$202B, EPS $1.96). Operating income: guide $22.5-26.5B. No sourced consensus; HSBC models $27B. AWS, the line the stock trades on, has a DISPUTED bar: 24/7 Wall St 2026-10-29 says $45.68B / +38%, while Pepperstone 2026-10-23 says ~35%. Q2 was +37% ($42.2B). So AWS-dependent findings are capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against the $202.2B revenue consensus.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 0.9% of float, 2.4 days to cover (FINRA settlement 2026-09-30, via https://tapeboard.com/stock/AMZN/short-squeeze). Not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. The baseline seal failed (status 'bars_failed: HTTPError'), so there is no sealed implied move or skew. Saxo (2026-10-27, https://www.home.saxo/content/articles/options/amazon-earnings-between-a-typical-report-and-julys-15-jump-27102026) priced the 250-strike Oct-30 straddle at $19.08, ~7.7% of the $249.09 close: put $9.90, call $9.18. With the put $0.91 in the money, that is roughly parity-neutral, so there is no visible put skew. Pepperstone cites ±7.4%. Price path (Yahoo chart): 254.60 on 10-28 to 245.07 at 14:15 ET 10-29 (−3.7% intraday on Alphabet's −12%). Run-up from the 2026-09-30 close of 249.15 is about −1.6%; from the 10-21 high of 262.37 it is −6.6%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was 'Bullish' with 'Extremely High' message volume on 2026-10-12.

evidence.text: Peer cloud prints since Amazon last spoke both beat on AI-cloud demand. Microsoft (10-28): Azure +48% to $33.17B against a ~45% guide and $32.32B consensus; next-quarter guide 49-50% cc against Street 45.1%; CFO: 'demand exceeds supply'. The same release cites third-party supply delays and capex below consensus at $45.2B. Alphabet (10-28): Google Cloud +103% to $30.7B, operating income $11.1B. The AMZN bar is AWS +35-38% on Q2's +37%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: AWS acceleration has driven the big up-moves: Q2 2026 AWS +37% (fastest in 18 quarters) took the stock +15.3%; Q3 2025 AWS reacceleration +9.6% (Saxo series). Beats without AWS acceleration were sold: −8.3% Q2 2025, −5.6% Q4 2025.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market were carrying the peer demand read into AMZN, the stock would have held or risen with MSFT's +4% after-hours. Instead it is −3.7% today and MSFT has given back to −2%. The market is pricing peers' capex and FCF, not their cloud growth rates. One counterweight is MSFT's third-party supply delays, which could equally cap AWS; that is netted into this size.
evidence.independence: Alphabet's own 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm, 2026-10-28) gives Cloud +103%. Two different companies, but both are proxies for AWS, not AWS's own number.

evidence.text: Anthropic, AWS's anchor AI customer with a >$100B 10-year AWS commitment and ~1GW of Trainium capacity due by end-2026, reached an annualized revenue run-rate above $65B by end-July 2026, more than 7x its end-2025 pace (Bloomberg, 2026-08-18). That is direct-counterparty demand inside AWS's Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same AWS line as above: +15.3% when AWS printed +37% in Q2 2026.
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-rate is public and is probably part of why the AWS bar moved from ~35% (Pepperstone 10-23) to ~38% (24/7 Wall St 10-29). That rising bar is the sign the market has partly priced it. What remains is whether AWS capacity let Amazon bill it. Jassy said in July that capacity will not meet all 2026 demand.
evidence.independence: Anthropic's own compute announcement (https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-amazon-compute, 2026-04-20) gives the 5GW / ~1GW-by-end-2026 Trainium schedule. Google Cloud's TPU-driven +103% shares the Anthropic-demand driver, so this partly overlaps the peer finding; it is sized small for that reason.

evidence.text: AMZN de-rated into the print on peer read-through: −3.7% intraday on 10-29 (254.60 to 245.07) as Alphabet fell ~12% on an EPS miss ($8.7B equity-securities loss), negative FCF and a signalled 2027 spend increase. That follows −4.6% on 10-22 in a sector AI sell-off. In July the same pattern (AMZN sold on Alphabet's capex shock) preceded a +15.3% print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: stock sold off on Alphabet's July capex read-through, then +15.3% on its own print. One precedent only; over 8 prints it is 4 up, 4 down, typical |move| ~6% (Saxo).
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a price fact, so it is the market's own statement. The question is whether the de-rating is about Amazon or about Alphabet's search miss and equity loss, which Amazon does not share. Amazon's consensus EPS excludes Anthropic marks (Pepperstone), so an Alphabet-style 'EPS miss on investment marks' cannot hit the Street number the same way. If the market had already discounted that difference, AMZN would not have fallen a third of Alphabet's move on a day MSFT and META held up.
evidence.independence: 24/7 Wall St 2026-10-29 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/amazon-slides-3-as-alphabets-12-plunge-raises-stakes-for-aws-report-meta-rises-3-microsoft-pulls-back/) attributes the AMZN drop to Alphabet; TickerSpark attributes 10-22 to a sector sell-off (https://tickerspark.ai/market/amazon-com-inc-amzn-drops-5-as-ai-stocks-sell-off-1792695973080).

evidence.text: Capex and 2027 spending signal risk. Amazon raised 2026 cash capex to ~$220B in July. Trailing FCF is −$7.6B, long-term debt is $128.9B (from $65.6B at year-end), and management gave no FCF-recovery date. On 10-28/29 the market punished Alphabet for negative FCF and a signalled 'significant' 2027 increase. Amazon's call will very likely carry a 2027 capex direction.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 print (Feb 2026), when the ~$200B 2026 capex guide shocked: −5.6% next day (Saxo), −9.7% over two days (Trefis). Q2 2026 capex raise to $220B came with an AWS beat and the stock rose +15.3%. So the capex line is sold when AWS does not accelerate with it.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the −3.7% today is this fear. Not fully priced, because no 2027 number exists yet. If the market had fully discounted a large 2027 step-up, AMZN would trade like GOOGL (−12), not −3.7. Financing question [sizing note removed]: the money buys capacity against a $496B AWS backlog and a 'not enough capacity for 2026' statement, which is why this is not sized larger. META raised capex the same week and rose 3%.
evidence.independence: Pepperstone 2026-10-23 (https://pepperstone.com/en/insights/market-analysis/equities/amazon-q3-2026-earnings-preview) gives the FCF, debt and capex figures. It shares the Alphabet read-through with the positioning finding, but the facts differ: price there, spending signal here.

evidence.text: Q2's operating income carried ~$1.15B that will not repeat: ~$551M of AWS energy-contract gains (in the 39.4% AWS margin) and ~$600M of IEEPA tariff refunds (CFO: 'the bulk' of what Amazon expects). The comparison for Q3's operating margin and AWS margin is flattered by that much.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved instance on this name; one-offs in the AWS margin have not been a line AMZN traded on.
evidence.why_not_priced: The company guided Q3 operating income ($22.5-26.5B) knowing these would not repeat, so this sits inside the guide. The only unpriced part is how much sell-side margin models extrapolated the 39.4% AWS margin; UBS's 46% 2027 AWS margin against a 39% consensus (24/7 Wall St) suggests most did not.
evidence.independence: Supply Chain Dive on the ~$600M refund and 'bulk received' (https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/amazon-to-issue-tariff-refunds-in-limited-set-of-circumstances/826815/).

evidence.text: HSBC (note 2026-10-12) models Q3 revenue $203.3B and operating income $27B, both above the top of guidance ($202B / $26.5B). It cites Amazon beating the top of its operating-profit guide for 15 consecutive quarters; separately, Amazon has beaten EPS in 11 of its last 12 reports (24/7 Wall St).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats are not paid on their own: 3 of the last 11 EPS beats saw the stock fall the next day (24/7 Wall St), and over 8 prints it is 4 up, 4 down.
evidence.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus already sits at the top of the guide ($202.2B), so the revenue part is priced. The operating-income beat pattern is less visible because no consensus OI number circulates in the previews, though a top-of-range OI print is the market's habit-based expectation. Sized small for that reason.
evidence.independence: 24/7 Wall St 2026-10-29 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/alphabet-failed-wall-streets-new-ai-test-amazon-takes-it-tonight/) gives the 11-of-12 beat record.

evidence.text: US card-panel proxy for retail: the Kalshi market on Carbon Arc's September 2026 Amazon card-spend index priced ~16-20% YoY growth (above-116 at ~98%, above-120 at ~8%) as of 2026-10-05. September is a clean month, since Prime Day moved into Q2, set against a total Q3 revenue guide of +9-12% depressed by the Prime Day shift and ~80bp FX.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Retail has not been the swing line recently; AWS is (Saxo, Pepperstone).
evidence.why_not_priced: Proxy: a prediction-market price on a third-party panel, not a settled reading or a company number, auto-generated page with internal inconsistencies. If the market believed strong September retail, revenue consensus would sit clearly above $202.2B rather than at the guide's top end.
evidence.independence: none

evidence.text: Amazon cut fewer than 1,000 more corporate roles on 2026-10-07, mostly in Stores (customer service, seller support, retail engineering), extending ~30,000 cuts since October 2025. That is a small cost item for Q4 opex.
evidence.source_date: 2026-10 (page; cuts confirmed 2026-10-07; secondary source, Amazon has not disclosed numbers)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measurable reaction attributable to the cost-cut line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Immaterial at Amazon's scale (<1,000 of ~1.5m employees). Filed for completeness.
evidence.independence: none

evidence.text: Investment marks: Amazon carried Anthropic at $190.4B at 30 June and booked a $53.4B pre-tax gain in Q2. Alphabet booked an $8.7B equity-securities LOSS in Q3 (−$0.55 EPS), unnamed. Amazon's GAAP EPS can swing tens of billions either way on Q3 marks, but consensus EPS excludes Anthropic marks (Pepperstone).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026's $53.4B gain came with +15.3%, but that move was attributed to AWS, not the mark.
evidence.why_not_priced: Below operating income, sign unknown (no Anthropic priced round found in Q3), with no path to guidance. Alphabet's loss shows headline-EPS misses on marks can trigger algorithmic selling after hours, which is the only reason it is filed. [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: Pepperstone 2026-10-23 (https://pepperstone.com/en/insights/market-analysis/equities/amazon-q3-2026-earnings-preview) on the $190.4B carrying value and consensus excluding marks.

Revenue sources agree within $0.5M; whisper EPS $0.27. Company FY26 guide $490-500M revenue, $66-78M adj. EBITDA (2026-07-30). H1 was $249.7M including ~$25M lab products (sold 2026-06-30), so the guide implies $120-125M a quarter in H2 and consensus sits at its midpoint.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 6.59M shares, 4.6 days to cover (aggregator snapshot dated 2026-10-26, https://equibles.com/stocks/cdna/shortinterest). That is ~12.7% of the 51.7M shares outstanding on 2026-07-27 (10-Q). The August snapshot read 6.1M, 11.9% of float, 4.3 days, so the short has edged up. Baseline: 25-delta skew null (not computable); put/call open interest 2.0 on 10,773 contracts; event-implied move 15.84%, but the ATM spread is 46% of mid, so indicative only. Spot $72.26 at the 52-week high, +9.1% over 20 days, +406% off the 52-week low, above the StockAnalysis mean target of $61.67 (range $46-75). Moderately crowded short into a momentum high.

evidence.text: The Q2 2026 10-Q (Note 2) shows CareDx recognized $18.0M in Q2 and $35.6M in H1 2026 of revenue for tests performed in prior periods, partly offset by $2.4M / $5.8M of refund-reserve increases. Net that is ~$14M in Q1 and ~$16M in Q2, so it has recurred two quarters running. A Q3 build without it (58,000 transplant tests guided × ~$1,450 core ASP ≈ $84M, NavDx ~$11-12M, Patient & Digital ~$19M) gives ~$115M, which means the $122.4M consensus carries only ~$7M of prior-period revenue. A third quarter at the Q1-Q2 rate would put revenue near $128-132M, about 5-8% above the bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (not pre-released): revenue $131.9M vs $114.1M consensus (+16%), with $16M prior-period revenue; stock +14.72% (baseline 2026-07-30). Q1 2026: $117.7M vs $102M consensus, but already pre-released on 2026-04-16 (+27.6% that day); the full print was -5.07%. Q4 2025: pre-released 2026-01-12 (+20.08%); full print 2026-02-24 -4.1%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at the guide midpoint, not at the Q1-Q2 run-rate including prior-period revenue. If the street modelled the collections as recurring, Q3 consensus would be near $128-130M rather than $122M. The quality question (prior-period revenue may be discounted as low quality) is why this is sized below the Q2 reaction.
evidence.independence: Q1 2026 release independently reports ~$14M of prior-period revenue (https://investors.caredx.com/news/news-details/2026/CareDx-Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx). Shares the prior-period logic with the EBITDA-guide finding below; the two are counted separately because one lands on the quarter and the other on the guide.

evidence.text: The FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide of $66-78M against H1 actuals of ~$44M (Q1 $19M + Q2 $24.8M) implies only $22-34M for all of H2, i.e. $11-17M a quarter, against $24.8M in Q2 alone. The revenue guide likewise implies $120-125M a quarter ex lab products, below the ~$119M ex-lab Q2 plus a NavDx quarter. The guide therefore looks built with zero prior-period revenue and a conservative NavDx margin, leaving room for a fourth consecutive raise (Feb $420-444M, Apr $447-465M, Jul $490-500M).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Every 2026 guide raise has come with a large move on the day it was first disclosed: the Jan 12 preliminary +20.1%, the Apr 16 preliminary +27.6%, the Jul 30 print with the $490-500M raise +14.7%. Raises that only confirmed a pre-release (Feb 24, Apr 28) were sold 4-5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Earnings Whispers preview (2026-10-21) frames H2 EBITDA as 'far below the Q2 level', i.e. the street reads the guide literally. If a raise were priced, consensus FY EBITDA and Q3 revenue would sit above the guide midpoint, not on it.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview makes the same H2 EBITDA arithmetic independently (https://finviz.com/news/406024/caredx-faces-first-navdx-quarter-with-street-estimates-trailing-its-raised-outlook). Shares the prior-period driver with the finding above.

evidence.text: The final Medicare LCD for solid-organ transplant molecular testing (published 2026-07-16, effective ~2026-08-30) allows up to 6 AlloSure Kidney surveillance tests in year 1 and 4 a year in years 2-3, up from 4 and 2 in the draft, and 12 a year for heart/lung in year 1. CareDx removed a previously expected $7.5M Medicare headwind from its guide. Q3 carries one month under the new policy; Q4 and 2027 commentary carry the rest.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The LCD finalization (2026-07-16) preceded the Q2 print, which rose +14.7% on a raise that included the removal of the $7.5M Medicare impact. BTIG's 2026-09-24 note on management's post-LCD confidence came with a ~14% one-day gain.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock is +63% since the Q2 print. What is not yet in numbers is the volume and ASP uplift from expanded surveillance frequency, which management has not quantified. A quantified 2027 frame on the call would be new; if it were priced, sell-side FY27 numbers would already reflect higher surveillance frequency.
evidence.independence: Natera (direct competitor, Prospera) said on its Q2 2026 call that the final LCD will benefit transplant volumes and ASPs in H2 2026 (https://www.tickerreport.com/?p=13537117). Medtech coverage of the final LCD: https://www.genomeweb.com/node/655691

evidence.text: Naveris (NavDx), acquired 2026-07-01, booked $10.8M revenue in Q1 2026 (8-K/A EX-99.2, filed 2026-09-16) and $34.3M in FY2025. CareDx's guide assumes ~$24M of specialty oncology revenue in H2 (~$12M a quarter) on 14,600 Q3 oncology tests at $770-795. The standalone run-rate already reaches that, so NavDx lands in line to slightly above. The 8-K/A also carries a going-concern note for standalone Naveris, which is moot under CareDx's ownership.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: First quarter with NavDx consolidated; no history on this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 8-K/A financials are not carried in previews. The contribution is small (~10% of revenue) and inside guide, hence the small size. The Q4 billing migration toward $1,000+ per test lands after the window.
evidence.independence: Naveris FY2025 $34.3M audited statements (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1217234/000121723426000052/naveris2025financialstat.htm); same filing, so one source.

evidence.text: Positioning into the print is stretched. Spot $72.26 is at the 52-week high, +9.1% over 20 days and ~+63% since the Q2 print, above the $61.67 mean analyst target (7 analysts, range $46-75). Whisper EPS $0.27 sits above the $0.24 consensus, and put/call open interest is 2.0. A beat in line with the last two quarters (+15-16% revenue) may already be what holders expect. Partly offset by ~12.7% of shares short (6.59M, 4.6 days), which is squeeze fuel on a clean raise.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prints that only confirmed known numbers (Feb 24, Apr 28) fell 4-5% even with beats; the un-pre-released Q2 rose 14.7% from a lower base.
evidence.why_not_priced: This finding is about what is priced: a stock above every average target with a whisper above consensus needs a beat plus raise larger than the last one. If expectations were modest, the stock would sit below targets and the whisper would equal consensus.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (2026-10-21) gives the $0.27 whisper and the +63% since the last print (https://finviz.com/news/406024/caredx-faces-first-navdx-quarter-with-street-estimates-trailing-its-raised-outlook); short interest from https://equibles.com/stocks/cdna/shortinterest

evidence.text: Company Q3 volume guide: 58,000 transplant tests (72,600 total including 14,600 specialty oncology), flat sequentially versus Q2's ~58,000. That compares with Q1 54,900 and Q2 58,000 (+17% YoY each), so transplant-volume growth decelerates sequentially, against a backdrop of declining US deceased-donor kidney transplants since mid-2025.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume has printed +17% YoY in each 2026 quarter; there has been no volume miss this year to measure.
evidence.why_not_priced: The volume target is public (raised from 56,600 to 58,000), so this is mostly priced. The residual is that ASP, not volume, is carrying growth, and a volume print at or below 58k would expose that.
evidence.independence: Kidney transplant decline in 2025 (proxy, not company-confirmed): https://californiainsider.com/news/kidney-transplants-drop-amid-increased-organ-donation-oversight-5971994

evidence.text: EDGAR shows 17 Form 144 proposed-sale notices from insiders between 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-17, right after the Q2 print, plus Form 4s on 2026-09-15 and five on 2026-10-05 (content not read). This is routine post-window selling into a +60% move; there is no open-market buy cluster.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: none measured
evidence.why_not_priced: Insider selling after a window opens is common and weakly informative; it is sized near zero for that reason.

evidence.text: BTIG met management in Boston in the week of 2026-09-22 and raised its target from $60 to $74 (Buy), reporting management 'confident' after the LCD resolution and strong core transplant growth. evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced (the +14% day). The residual is that management spoke confidently with ~one week of Q3 left, which lowers the probability of a negative surprise, not the size of the upside.

evidence.text: Columbia beat its own revenue guidance and consensus in both reported 2026 quarters. Q1 revenue was $779.0m vs a $755.6m consensus, with EPS $0.65 vs $0.35. Q2 revenue was $614.4m vs ~$607m. Consensus for Q3 ($938-942.5m, EPS $1.25-1.28) sits at the top of the $929-943m revenue guide and the middle of the $1.15-1.35 EPS guide. Management said the >$30m Q3-to-Q4 shift is timing, 'not a function of any cancellations', and that there were 'no changes in our order book for fall 2026'. A modest beat on the quarter is the base case, at about +1% revenue vs bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 beat with raised op-income guide: +2.35%. Q2 2026 beat on revenue with a soft Q3 guide: -5.43%. 5 of the last 7 prints fell, so this name has not reliably paid for quarterly beats.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The whisper ($1.31) is already above consensus, and consensus sits at the top of the revenue guide. If the market expected a large beat, the whisper would sit at or above the $1.35 top of guide. It does not.
evidence.independence: Q2 beat in the Q2 exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050797/000105079726000129/colmfy26q2exhibit991.htm). The 'no cancellations / no change in fall order book' quote is from the Q2 call (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1949254-20260731). These are company sources, not independent ones.

evidence.text: Input costs worsened after the July guide. On the Q2 call the CFO flagged incremental outbound freight charges and fuel pressure, and cited oil 'in the $90-$100 range' as a fall 2027 headwind. Brent has held above $100 since late September ($103.50 on Oct 12), and the EIA's October outlook puts Q4 2026 Brent at $104.69. Tanker freight stays elevated after strikes near Hormuz. This raises the risk that the H2 margin guide (FY op margin 8.5-9.3%) is trimmed or that the early 2027 margin commentary is cautious.
evidence.source_date: 2026-10 (EIA October STEO; URL path undated, content refers to the Q4 2026 forecast)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: 'H2 outlook incrementally moderated' plus a Q3 guide below the Street gave -5.43%. Q2 2025 (2025-07-31): -12.85% on a weak outlook. Guidance cuts have been punished hard.
evidence.why_not_priced: Sell-side targets were cut after Q2 (Stifel $67, Baird $65), but the stock has since rallied 10% in 20 days to $63.5, near those targets. That rally does not look like a market discounting a margin cut from above-$100 oil. If this were priced, the stock would have drifted lower with crude from late September.
evidence.independence: This is a proxy: macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed since July. Brent >$100 since late Sep is in a separate source (https://www.procurementresource.com/news-and-articles/brent-crude-oil-falls-to-103-50-dollars-per-barrel). The company's own sensitivity comes from the Q2 call (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1949254-20260731).

evidence.text: NOAA's 2026-27 Winter Outlook (Oct 16) projects a very strong El Nino with warmer-than-average temperatures across much of the northern US for Dec-Feb. This lands on the quarter Columbia's guide leans on. The FY guide implies Q4 sales of about $1.09-1.18bn: FY $3.43-3.50bn less Q1 $779.0m, Q2 $614.4m and the Q3 guide. That is roughly +6% at the midpoint including the >$30m shifted shipments, against about 4-5% underlying per the CFO. CEO Boyle on the Q2 call: 'the weather tends to be much more impactful than almost any economic indicator.' A cautious Q4 framing or a FY sales trim is the risk.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 outlook prints: 2025-10-30 -3.63% and 2025-07-31 -12.85% on weak outlooks. Feb 2026 +14.44% when the FY26 guide surprised up. The guide moves this name more than the quarter does.
evidence.why_not_priced: The outlook was public on Oct 16, and the stock has risen since (+2.3% over 5 days). Retail-weather risk is not visible in the price or in the sell-side targets. Partly priced through the +4.85 downside skew.
evidence.independence: This is a weather proxy, not confirmed by the company. Mid/late-October cold in the Northeast (https://weatheronthisday.com/trends/halloween-weather-forecast-2026) runs the other way for October sell-through. The Q4 arithmetic uses the company's own guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050797/000105079726000129/colmfy26q2exhibit991.htm).

evidence.text: A direct outerwear peer reported on Oct 28, after Columbia last spoke. VF's The North Face grew 4% in the quarter to Sep 26, with Americas +8%. Timberland Americas grew +15%. Americas ex-Dickies grew +6% 'reflecting sustained growth across channels'. VF guided TNF Q3 (Oct-Dec) to +4% or better, said it feels 'really, really good about Q3, Q4', and built inventory +7% 'to support demand in H2'. That is evidence that US outdoor/outerwear wholesale and DTC demand held through September. It supports Columbia's guided return to US wholesale growth in H2, weighted to Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No COLM-specific history on peer reads. COLM's US business fell 4% in Q2 and 8% in H1 while TNF Americas grew 8% in H1, so Columbia has been losing share. The read-through is weaker than a like-for-like.
evidence.why_not_priced: It came out one session before COLM's print, and COLM consensus ($1.25-1.28, $938-942m) has not moved off the July guide midpoint. A stale bar is the pattern that has paid. Netted: VF said part of TNF's quarter was wholesale pulled forward from its Q3. Columbia's own US business has lagged TNF all year (net of share loss).
evidence.independence: The VF Q2 FY27 call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/28/vf-vfc-q2-2027-earnings-call-transcript/) is the same company and event, so it is one source. No independent corroboration.

evidence.text: Counterparties point to a promotional, mixed fall. Dick's (Columbia's large wholesale partner) cut its FY EPS guide to $11.00-12.00 from $13.50-14.50 in late August, citing 'increasingly promotional conditions across portions of the athletic footwear and apparel marketplace'. Deckers (Oct 22) grew UGG only +3.5%, with DTC -1.8%. Columbia's CFO already built 'continued promotions' and 'more consumer pressure' into the H2 gross-margin assumptions.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin/guide disappointments: -5.43% (Q2 2026), -12.85% (Q2 2025).
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Dick's was public two months ago, and Columbia's guide already assumes promotions. The residual is that Deckers' DTC decline (Oct 22) is newer than any COLM estimate revision.
evidence.independence: Deckers Q2 FY27 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910521/000091052126000028/deckex991pressrelease-9302.htm), a different company and source. Partly offset by VF's stronger read (finding 4).
